properties.natural_language: Before verifying a sync aggregate BLS signature (ACTION-VERIFY-SYNC-SIGNATURE), the system MUST have successfully resolved the current sync committee of exactly 512 validators for the slot and aggregated the BLS public keys of participating members according to the participation bits. The aggregation optimization strategy (full committee, subtract non-participants if >256 participated, or direct aggregation if ≤256) must be correctly applied based on the participation count.

Throughout sync aggregate processing, the 512 participation bits MUST correspond one-to-one with the 512 validators in the current sync committee. The aggregated BLS public key MUST be cryptographically derivable from exactly the set of validators whose participation bits are set to 1. If all 512 bits are set, the precomputed full committee aggregate public key MAY be used as an optimization.

After successful verification of the sync aggregate BLS signature (STATE-SYNC-AGGREGATE-VALID), all participating sync committee members MUST receive their proportional share of the sync committee reward (SYNC_COMMITTEE_WEIGHT=2/64 of total rewards / 512 / 32 per slot), all non-participating members MUST receive equal penalties, and the block proposer MUST receive an additional reward proportional to PROPOSER_WEIGHT / (WEIGHT_DENOMINATOR - PROPOSER_WEIGHT). The total rewards and penalties MUST be atomically applied to validator balances.

A sync committee member who is slashed between committee selection (at sync period boundary) and their duty period MUST still appear in the sync committee membership list, but their signatures MUST NOT count toward valid aggregates and they MUST receive penalties for non-participation even if they attempt to sign.

Before updating participation flags for an attestation (ACTION-UPDATE-PARTICIPATION-FLAGS), the system MUST have evaluated all three timeliness conditions: source timeliness (inclusion delay ≤ integer_squareroot(SLOTS_PER_EPOCH)), target timeliness (inclusion delay ≤ SLOTS_PER_EPOCH), and head timeliness (inclusion in immediately next slot). Each flag MUST only be set if its corresponding timeliness condition is satisfied.

After attestation processing completes (STATE-ATTESTATION-PROCESSED), the proposer reward MUST be calculated as the sum over all attesting validators of: for each newly-set participation flag, the flag weight (TIMELY_SOURCE_WEIGHT=14, TIMELY_TARGET_WEIGHT=26, TIMELY_HEAD_WEIGHT=14 out of WEIGHT_DENOMINATOR=64) multiplied by the validator's base reward, scaled by the proposer reward fraction. The proposer MUST receive this reward atomically with flag updates.

Before computing inactivity penalties (ACTION-COMPUTE-INACTIVITY-PENALTIES), the system MUST have updated all validator inactivity scores according to the dual-decrement rule: if the validator missed the target vote, increment score by INACTIVITY_SCORE_BIAS=4; if not in leak mode, decrement by min(1, current_score); always decrement by min(INACTIVITY_SCORE_RECOVERY_RATE=16, current_score). The updated scores MUST be used for penalty calculation.

During inactivity leak periods, each validator's inactivity penalty MUST be computed as: (effective_balance * inactivity_score) / (INACTIVITY_SCORE_BIAS * INACTIVITY_PENALTY_QUOTIENT=50331648). This creates a quadratic relationship between leak duration and total penalties accumulated. The penalty MUST only apply to validators who failed to make a correct target vote.

After applying rewards and penalties (STATE-BALANCES-UPDATED), every validator's balance MUST reflect: (1) flag-based rewards for TIMELY_SOURCE, TIMELY_TARGET, and TIMELY_HEAD participation weighted 14, 26, and 14 respectively out of 64; (2) penalties for non-participation in each flag; (3) inactivity penalties if applicable; and (4) all balance changes MUST be applied atomically to prevent partial state updates.

Before rotating sync committees (ACTION-ROTATE-COMMITTEES), the system MUST be at an epoch that is a multiple of EPOCHS_PER_SYNC_COMMITTEE_PERIOD=256, MUST have computed the next sync committee by probabilistically selecting 512 validators weighted by effective balance using the RANDAO seed from exactly EPOCHS_PER_SYNC_COMMITTEE_PERIOD + 1 epochs ago, and MUST have constructed the SyncCommittee object with all 512 public keys and the precomputed aggregate public key.

The RANDAO seed used for sync committee selection MUST be derived from a point in time that is sufficiently far in the past (EPOCHS_PER_SYNC_COMMITTEE_PERIOD + 1 epochs before the period boundary) to prevent attackers from manipulating RANDAO to bias committee composition. The selection algorithm MUST produce a cryptographically unpredictable distribution of validators weighted by their effective balance.

Before determining whether reserve pricing mode applies (ACTION-COMPARE-FEES), the block producer MUST compute the reserve price as: reserve = (BLOB_BASE_COST * base_fee_per_gas) / GAS_PER_BLOB, where BLOB_BASE_COST=8192 and GAS_PER_BLOB=131072. The comparison MUST evaluate whether (BLOB_BASE_COST * base_fee) > (GAS_PER_BLOB * blob_base_fee) to select between reserve and normal pricing modes.

After excess blob gas calculation completes (STATE-EXCESS-BLOB-GAS-COMPUTED), if reserve mode was active (reserve condition true), excess MUST equal: parent_excess + blob_gas_used * (max - target) / max with no subtraction of target; if normal mode was active, excess MUST equal: parent_excess + blob_gas_used - target_blob_gas. Validators MUST independently recalculate this value and reject blocks where the header excess_blob_gas does not match.

The blob base fee MUST never fall below the reserve price floor defined by the ratio (BLOB_BASE_COST / GAS_PER_BLOB) = 1/16 of the execution gas base fee. When reserve pricing mode is active, excess blob gas MUST accumulate without subtraction of the target, preventing the blob base fee from decreasing below this threshold. This maintains economic alignment between blob costs and execution costs.

Before validating a block's excess_blob_gas header field (ACTION-COMPARE-HEADER), the validator MUST recalculate excess blob gas using the modified calc_excess_blob_gas function with reserve price logic applied to the parent block's state. The recalculation MUST use the exact same reserve condition evaluation and formula selection (reserve vs normal mode) that the block producer used.

At the EIP-7918 fork activation block, the new blobSchedule parameters from EIP-7840 (target and max blob gas values) MUST be applied immediately and atomically. The reserve price mechanism MUST activate simultaneously. There MUST be no transition period or gradual rollout; the fork block and all subsequent blocks MUST use the new parameters and reserve price logic.

Before processing any Beacon API request (ACTION-PROCESS-API-REQUEST), the node operator MUST have deployed additional security layers (reverse proxy with authentication, firewall rules, or network isolation) if the API is exposed to untrusted networks. The API implementation itself provides no built-in authentication or rate limiting. Endpoints that trigger heavy computation (state queries, validator duties) or return large responses (full beacon state) are vulnerable to DoS attacks without these external protections.

When the Beacon API is exposed without additional security layers (STATE-REQUEST-UNAUTHENTICATED), the node is vulnerable to denial-of-service attacks through multiple endpoints. An attacker can exhaust node resources by requesting expensive state computations, full beacon state downloads, or validator duty calculations. The API MUST NOT be exposed to the public internet without infrastructure-level protections.

Before routing an API request to a handler (ACTION-ROUTE-TO-HANDLER), the system MUST parse the HTTP request to extract method, path, headers, query parameters, and optional JSON body. The path and method combination MUST be matched against the OpenAPI 3 specification to identify the appropriate handler. If no matching handler exists, the request MUST be rejected with a route-not-found error rather than processed.

Before processing state changes under Shanghai fork rules (ACTION-PROCESS-STATE-CHANGE), the system MUST have successfully applied the fork transition (ACTION-APPLY-FORK) at the activation block. The fork transition performs irregular state changes that prepare the blockchain for Shanghai-specific features. All subsequent blocks MUST operate under Shanghai rules, including SELFDESTRUCT behavior changes (EIP-6780) and any other Shanghai-specific validations.

Before executing a transaction (ACTION-EXECUTE-TX), the system MUST validate that the transaction satisfies all Shanghai-specific rules including: valid signature verification, correct nonce sequencing, sufficient balance to cover gas costs and value transfer, proper transaction type encoding, and any Shanghai-specific constraints. A transaction that fails validation MUST transition to STATE-TX-REJECTED and MUST NOT be executed.

State transitions MUST be atomic: either a transaction executes completely and all state changes are committed, or it fails and all state changes are reverted. Partial state updates that leave the world state in an inconsistent condition MUST NOT occur. This atomicity guarantee applies to account balance changes, storage updates, code deployments, and all other state modifications.

Before preparing the VM for block execution (STATE-VM-READY), the block header MUST be validated (ACTION-VALIDATE-BLOCK-HEADER) to ensure: parent hash correctly references the previous block, timestamp is greater than parent timestamp, gas limit is within allowed bounds, and all Shanghai-specific header fields are properly formatted. Invalid block headers MUST be rejected before any execution begins.

Before requesting proof generation from the proof engine (ACTION-REQUEST-PROOF-GENERATION), the prover MUST extract all necessary execution payload data from the beacon block including: the execution payload itself, versioned hashes derived from blob KZG commitments, parent beacon block root, and execution requests. All ProofAttributes MUST be correctly assembled. Missing or malformed data MUST prevent proof generation from proceeding.

Before signing an execution proof with BLS (ACTION-SIGN-PROOF), the prover MUST validate the proof received from the proof engine to ensure it correctly attests to the execution payload validity. The signature MUST be computed using domain separation with DOMAIN_EXECUTION_PROOF and the current epoch to prevent cross-domain and cross-epoch signature replay attacks. A prover MUST NOT blindly sign proof engine output without validation.

The proof engine output crosses a trust boundary between the external proof generation engine and the prover. Even if co-located, the proof engine is a separate component whose output MUST be cryptographically validated before being signed. A compromised or buggy proof engine could produce invalid proofs that, once signed by a whitelisted prover, would deceive stateless validators into accepting invalid blocks.

Before accepting an execution proof for stateless validation (STATE-PROOF-VALIDATED), the proof MUST pass all validation checks in sequence: (1) proof data field is non-empty, (2) proof engine cryptographically verifies the proof correctness, (3) no duplicate proof with the same request root and proof type has been received, and (4) the BLS signature on the SignedExecutionProof is valid for a whitelisted prover using DOMAIN_EXECUTION_PROOF. Failure of any check MUST result in proof rejection.

After a stateless validator uses a validated execution proof for block validation (ACTION-STATELESS-VALIDATE-BLOCK), the beacon block's execution payload MUST be verified as valid without requiring the validator to run a full execution layer client. The proof cryptographically guarantees correct state transition execution. If sufficient whitelisted provers fail to provide proofs in a timely manner, stateless validators cannot validate blocks and may miss attestations.

Only whitelisted provers are authorized to generate and sign execution proofs. The whitelisting mechanism provides a trust boundary: proofs signed by non-whitelisted participants MUST be rejected during BLS signature verification. An attacker who cannot forge BLS signatures of whitelisted provers MUST NOT be able to inject fraudulent execution proofs into the gossip network that would be accepted by stateless validators.
Before executing SELFDESTRUCT opcode, the contract must be in an executing state with valid contract address and target address available in the execution context
When SELFDESTRUCT is encountered, the EVM must accurately track whether the contract was created in the same transaction by maintaining creation transaction identifiers throughout execution

The same-transaction creation determination must be consistent and deterministic - if a contract was created via CREATE or CREATE2 in the current transaction, it must always be detected as same-TX creation regardless of call depth or internal call patterns
After SELFDESTRUCT on a same-transaction created contract, the contract state (storage, code, account) must be completely deleted and balance must be zeroed, resulting in STATE-CONTRACT-DESTROYED
After SELFDESTRUCT on a pre-existing contract (not created in same transaction), the contract code and storage must persist unchanged, with only the balance transferred to the target address

Execution must always halt after SELFDESTRUCT processing completes, regardless of whether the contract was destroyed or persists, ensuring no further opcodes execute in the selfdestructed contract context
After SELFDESTRUCT in non-same-transaction context, no gas refund shall be issued, and EIP-2929 access list gas rules must apply instead of legacy refund mechanisms
Ether burning via self-targeting SELFDESTRUCT requires that the contract was created in the same transaction and the target address equals the executing contract address

Before transaction validation proceeds, the transaction type byte must be recognized as one of the valid EIP-2718 types (0=legacy, 1=EIP-2930, 2=EIP-1559, 3=EIP-4844 blob, 4=EIP-7702 auth), otherwise TransactionTypeError must be raised
For blob transactions (type 3), contract creation (to=None) must be disallowed and raise TransactionTypeContractCreationError before fee validation proceeds
Transaction fee structure validation requires maxFeePerGas >= block baseFeePerGas AND maxPriorityFeePerGas <= maxFeePerGas, with violations raising InsufficientMaxFee or PriorityFeeError respectively
Blob transactions must contain at least one blob (non-empty blob data), otherwise NoBlobDataError must be raised before versioned hash validation
All blob versioned hashes must have a valid version prefix byte, blob gas usage must not exceed the per-block maximum, and maxFeePerBlobGas must be sufficient for the current blob base fee
Contract creation initialization code size must not exceed MAX_INITCODE_SIZE, otherwise InitCodeTooLargeError must be raised before execution begins
Authorization list transactions (EIP-7702 type 4) must contain a non-empty authorization list, otherwise EmptyAuthorizationListError must be raised
Exception handlers must be invoked correctly for all validation failures and must not be bypassable through malformed input or edge cases, ensuring invalid transactions are always rejected
When upgrading from eth/66 to eth/67, the protocol upgrade action must atomically disable both GetNodeData (0x0d) and NodeData (0x0e) message types before processing any eth/67 messages
Upon receiving a wire protocol message, eth/67 clients must check message type and reject deprecated GetNodeData (0x0d) or NodeData (0x0e) messages before processing content
After rejecting a deprecated message type, the client should either ignore the message or disconnect the peer for protocol violation, ensuring no processing of unsupported message types

When a client needs state/code data and the peer supports only eth/67, the client must use snap protocol (GetByteCodes 0x04 for contract code or GetTrieNodes 0x06 for trie nodes) instead of deprecated GetNodeData
During the transition period, sufficient eth/66 or snap-capable peers must be available in the network to allow syncing nodes to obtain state data, otherwise state synchronization will fail
The snap protocol must provide equivalent security properties to GetNodeData for state retrieval, with no new attack vectors introduced by the migration

Before processing a merge transition block, the system must verify it is the first beacon block with a non-empty execution payload (is_merge_transition_block condition: pre-state has no execution and block contains non-empty payload)

Terminal PoW block validation requires fetching block data via eth_getBlockByHash and verifying either (total_difficulty >= TERMINAL_TOTAL_DIFFICULTY AND parent_total_difficulty < TERMINAL_TOTAL_DIFFICULTY) OR (if TERMINAL_BLOCK_HASH set: exact hash match at epoch >= TERMINAL_BLOCK_HASH_ACTIVATION_EPOCH)
After successful merge transition validation, the beacon chain must permanently transition to managing execution payloads with PoS active, and PoW must no longer be the canonical execution mechanism

PoW block data must be available via eth_getBlockByHash during the merge transition window; if unavailable, blocks must be deferred for reprocessing (graceful degradation) rather than rejected, preventing permanent fork

An attacker must not be able to manipulate PoW chain total difficulty to trigger a premature or fraudulent merge transition, as this would anchor the beacon chain to attacker-controlled execution state

Before notifying the execution engine of fork choice updates, the consensus layer must compute safe_execution_block_hash from the justified checkpoint, ensuring all three hashes (head, safe, finalized) are ready for atomic update
After forkchoiceUpdated is sent to the execution engine, finalized payloads must be irreversibly persisted and the execution chain must reorganize to match the consensus head atomically

Fork choice update suppression via should_override_forkchoice_update requires ALL 8 conditions to be simultaneously true at a single point in time: head_late, proposing_reorg_slot, ffg_competitive, finalization_ok, and weak_head_strong_parent checks

After all re-org protection conditions are met, fork choice update must be suppressed to allow the proposer to build on the parent block instead of the late head, preventing single-slot reorganizations

Before processing any RPC method, the request must successfully pass JSON parsing, RPC structure validation (jsonrpc, method, id fields), method lookup, and parameter validation (Quantity/Data encoding rules with 0x prefix)
Quantity parameters must use minimal hex encoding (no leading zeros except 0x0), and Data parameters must have even hex digits (complete bytes), otherwise InvalidParams error (-32602) must be raised

All RPC errors must be mapped to standard error codes (-32700 parse, -32600 invalid request, -32601 method not found, -32602 invalid params, -32603 internal, -32000 to -32005 custom) with appropriate error response format
Raw transaction submission via eth_sendRawTransaction requires sequential validation: hex decode, RLP decode, ECDSA signature verification with sender recovery, before mempool acceptance
After successful signature validation and mempool acceptance, the transaction hash (32-byte keccak256) must be returned to the client, confirming the transaction is awaiting block inclusion

Invalid transaction signatures must always be rejected before mempool insertion, preventing unauthorized transaction submission even with RPC access, as signature forgery is cryptographically infeasible

RPC endpoints must not be exposed publicly without infrastructure-level protections (rate limiting, authentication, firewall), as the specification provides no built-in DoS or authentication mechanisms
Sensitive operations like eth_sign require transport-layer security (HTTPS/WSS) to prevent man-in-the-middle attacks intercepting or modifying signing requests
